sanskrit: kṣattar yad gurur ācāryo bravīti kuru tat tathā na hīdṛśaṃ priyaṃ manye bhavitā dharmavatsala
english: O Kṣattṛ, whatever the preceptor and teacher commands, carry it out accordingly; I think there will be no joy equal to this, O cherisher of dharma.

sanskrit: tato rājānam āmantrya vidurānugato bahiḥ bhāradvājo mahāprājño māpayām āsa medinīm samām avṛkṣāṃ nirgulmām udakpravaṇasaṃsthitām
english: Then, taking leave of the king and accompanied by Vidura, the supremely wise son of Bharadvaja went outside and measured out a level ground, free of trees and shrubs, situated near a slope with access to water.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ bhūmau baliṃ cakre tithau nakṣatrapūjite avaghuṣṭaṃ pure cāpi tadarthaṃ vadatāṃ vara
english: On that ground, on a lunar day when the asterism was auspicious and was duly worshipped, he performed the consecrating oblation; and a proclamation was also announced throughout the city for that purpose, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: raṅgabhūmau suvipulaṃ śāstradṛṣṭaṃ yathāvidhi prekṣāgāraṃ suvihitaṃ cakrus tatra ca śilpinaḥ rājñaḥ sarvāyudhopetaṃ strīṇāṃ caiva nararṣabha
english: On the tournament ground, craftsmen duly constructed a very spacious arena in accordance with the prescriptions of the treatises, well appointed and equipped with all weapons for the king and the ladies as well, O bull among men.

sanskrit: mañcāṃś ca kārayām āsus tatra jānapadā janāḥ vipulān ucchrayopetāñ śibikāś ca mahādhanāḥ
english: The people of the countryside also had great platforms raised there, broad and lofty, as well as richly adorned palanquins.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tato 'hani prāpte rājā sasacivas tadā bhīṣmaṃ pramukhataḥ kṛtvā kṛpaṃ cācāryasattamam
english: When that day arrived, the king together with his ministers, placing Bhīṣma foremost and Kṛpa the best of teachers beside him,

sanskrit: muktājālaparikṣiptaṃ vaiḍūryamaṇibhūṣitam śātakumbhamayaṃ divyaṃ prekṣāgāram upāgamat
english: proceeded to the divine viewing pavilion draped with nets of pearls, adorned with lapis lazuli gems, and fashioned from pure gold.

sanskrit: gāndhārī ca mahābhāgā kuntī ca jayatāṃ vara striyaś ca sarvā yā rājñaḥ sapreṣyāḥ saparicchadāḥ harṣād āruruhur mañcān meruṃ devastriyo yathā
english: The illustrious Gāndhārī and Kuntī, O best of the victorious, together with all the royal ladies, their attendants and retinues, ascended the platforms with joy, like the divine women ascending Mount Meru.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇakṣatriyādyaṃ ca cāturvarṇyaṃ purād drutam darśanepsu samabhyāgāt kumārāṇāṃ kṛtāstratām
english: The four social orders headed by brahmins and kshatriyas came quickly from the city, eager to witness the weapons-mastery of the princes.

sanskrit: pravāditaiś ca vāditrair janakautūhalena ca mahārṇava iva kṣubdhaḥ samājaḥ so 'bhavat tadā
english: With musical instruments sounding and the eager curiosity of the people, that assembly became agitated at that time like a great ocean.

sanskrit: tataḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklayajñopavītavān śuklakeśaḥ sitaśmaśruḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ
english: Then, wearing white garments, with a white sacred thread, white hair, white beard, and anointed with white garlands and unguents,

sanskrit: raṅgamadhyaṃ tadācāryaḥ saputraḥ praviveśa ha nabho jaladharair hīnaṃ sāṅgāraka ivāṃśumān
english: that teacher entered the middle of the arena together with his son, like the sun with Mars entering a sky bereft of clouds.

sanskrit: sa yathāsamayaṃ cakre baliṃ balavatāṃ varaḥ brāhmaṇāṃś cātra mantrajñān vācayām āsa maṅgalam
english: He, the best among the mighty, performed the consecrating rites in the proper seasonal manner and had brahmins versed in sacred formulas recite auspicious hymns there.

sanskrit: atha puṇyāhaghoṣasya puṇyasya tadanantaram viviśur vividhaṃ gṛhya śastropakaraṇaṃ narāḥ
english: Immediately after the proclamation of that auspicious day, warriors entered carrying various kinds of weapons and equipment.

sanskrit: tato baddhatanutrāṇā baddhakakṣyā mahābalāḥ baddhatūṇāḥ sadhanuṣo viviśur bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Then the mighty bulls of the Bhārata line entered, their armor fastened, their girdles tied, their quivers strapped on, bows in hand.

sanskrit: anujyeṣṭhaṃ ca te tatra yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ cakrur astraṃ mahāvīryāḥ kumārāḥ paramādbhutam
english: Those princes of great valor, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, in order of seniority, performed feats of arms there that were most wondrous.

sanskrit: ke cic charākṣepabhayāc chirāṃsy avananāmire manujā dhṛṣṭam apare vīkṣāṃ cakruḥ savismayāḥ
english: Some in the crowd bowed their heads in fear of being struck by arrows; others gazed boldly with astonishment.

sanskrit: te sma lakṣyāṇi vividhur bāṇair nāmāṅkaśobhitaiḥ vividhair lāghavotsṛṣṭair uhyando vājibhir drutam
english: They pierced various targets with arrows embellished with their names, shot with skillful dexterity in diverse ways, while being carried swiftly on horses.

sanskrit: tat kumārabalaṃ tatra gṛhītaśarakārmukam gandharvanagarākāraṃ prekṣya te vismitābhavan
english: Seeing that assembled force of princes there with bows and arrows in hand, arrayed like a city of the gandharvas, those onlookers were struck with wonder.

sanskrit: sahasā cukruśus tatra narāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ vismayotphullanayanāḥ sādhu sādhv iti bhārata
english: Hundreds of thousands of men suddenly burst out shouting there, their eyes wide with amazement, "Excellent! Excellent!" O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṛtvā dhanuṣi te mārgān rathacaryāsu cāsakṛt gajapṛṣṭhe 'śvapṛṣṭhe ca niyuddhe ca mahābalāḥ
english: Having demonstrated their skills repeatedly with the bow, in chariot-driving, on the back of elephants, on the back of horses, and in close combat, those mighty ones,

sanskrit: gṛhītakhaḍgacarmāṇas tato bhūyaḥ prahāriṇaḥ tsarumārgān yathoddiṣṭāṃś ceruḥ sarvāsu bhūmiṣu
english: then again taking sword and shield as combatants, moved through the prescribed sword-paths on all terrains as instructed.

sanskrit: lāghavaṃ sauṣṭhavaṃ śobhāṃ sthiratvaṃ dṛḍhamuṣṭitām dadṛśus tatra sarveṣāṃ prayoge khaḍgacarmaṇām
english: In the use of sword and shield, the spectators there observed in all of them swiftness, elegance of form, beauty, steadiness, and firmness of grip.

sanskrit: atha tau nityasaṃhṛṣṭau suyodhanavṛkodarau avatīrṇau gadāhastāv ekaśṛṅgāv ivācalau
english: Then those two ever-exuberant ones, Suyodhana and Vṛkodara, descended into the arena with maces in hand, like two mountains with a single peak.

sanskrit: baddhakakṣyau mahābāhū pauruṣe paryavasthitau bṛṃhantau vāśitāhetoḥ samadāv iva kuñjarau
english: Their girdles fastened, those two long-armed heroes, intent on displaying their manhood, roared like two musth elephants competing for a cow in heat.

sanskrit: tau pradakṣiṇasavyāni maṇḍalāni mahābalau ceratur nirmalagadau samadāv iva govṛṣau
english: Those two mighty ones with gleaming maces wheeled through circular maneuvers to the right and to the left, like two bulls of equal strength.

sanskrit: viduro dhṛtarāṣṭrāya gāndhāryai pāṇḍavāraṇiḥ nyavedayetāṃ tat sarvaṃ kumārāṇāṃ viceṣṭitam
english: Vidura and the offspring of Pāṇḍu's wife reported all the activities of the princes, the one to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the other to Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kururāje ca raṅgasthe bhīme ca balināṃ vare pakṣapātakṛtasnehaḥ sa dvidhevābhavaj janaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With the king of the Kurus and Bhīma, the foremost of the mighty, both present in the arena, that crowd, whose affections were divided by partiality, became as if split in two.

sanskrit: hā vīra kururājeti hā bhīmeti ca nardatām puruṣāṇāṃ suvipulāḥ praṇādāḥ sahasotthitāḥ
english: Loud, swelling cries of men suddenly arose, shouting "Ah, hero, king of the Kurus!" and "Ah, Bhīma!"

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣubdhārṇavanibhaṃ raṅgam ālokya buddhimān bhāradvājaḥ priyaṃ putram aśvatthāmānam abravīt
english: Then the wise son of Bharadvaja, seeing the arena resembling a turbulent ocean, spoke to his beloved son Aśvatthāman:

sanskrit: vārayaitau mahāvīryau kṛtayogyāv ubhāv api mā bhūd raṅgaprakopo 'yaṃ bhīmaduryodhanodbhavaḥ
english: "Restrain these two of great valor, both of whom are trained and ready; let there not be an uproar in the arena arising from Bhīma and Duryodhana."

sanskrit: tatas tāv udyatagadau guruputreṇa vāritau yugāntānilasaṃkṣubdhau mahāvegāv ivārṇavau
english: Then those two, with maces raised and of great momentum, were restrained by the teacher's son, like two oceans churned by the wind at the end of a cosmic age.

sanskrit: tato raṅgāṅgaṇagato droṇo vacanam abravīt nivārya vāditragaṇaṃ mahāmeghanibhasvanam
english: Then Droṇa, standing in the arena ground, silencing the orchestra whose sound was like that of a great thunder-cloud, spoke these words:

sanskrit: yo me putrāt priyataraḥ sarvāstraviduṣāṃ varaḥ aindrir indrānujasamaḥ sa pārtho dṛśyatām iti
english: "Let that Pārtha be seen, who is dearer to me than my own son, the best of all who know the science of weapons, the son of Indra, equal to Indra's younger brother."

sanskrit: ācāryavacanenātha kṛtasvastyayano yuvā baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇaḥ pūrṇatūṇaḥ sakārmukaḥ
english: At the teacher's word, that youth, having duly performed the benedictory rites, with arm-guard and finger-guard fastened, quiver full, and bow in hand,

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ kavacaṃ bibhrat pratyadṛśyata phalgunaḥ sārkaḥ sendrāyudhataḍit sasaṃdhya iva toyadaḥ
english: wearing his golden armor, Phalguna appeared like a rain-cloud with the sun, with Indra's rainbow, with lightning, and with the evening glow.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvasya raṅgasya samutpiñjo 'bhavan mahān prāvādyanta ca vādyāni saśaṅkhāni samantataḥ
english: Then a great tumultuous uproar arose from the entire arena, and musical instruments with conch shells sounded on all sides.

sanskrit: eṣa kuntīsutaḥ śrīmān eṣa pāṇḍavamadhyamaḥ eṣa putro mahendrasya kurūṇām eṣa rakṣitā
english: "This is the glorious son of Kuntī, this is the middle of the Pāṇḍava brothers, this is the son of the great Indra, this is the protector of the Kurus!"

sanskrit: eṣo 'straviduṣāṃ śreṣṭha eṣa dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ eṣa śīlavatāṃ cāpi śīlajñānanidhiḥ paraḥ
english: "This is the greatest among those learned in arms, this is the best of those who uphold dharma, and this too among those of good character is the supreme treasure-house of character and knowledge."

sanskrit: ity evam atulā vācaḥ śṛṇvantyāḥ prekṣakeritāḥ kuntyāḥ prasnavasaṃmiśrair asraiḥ klinnam uro 'bhavat
english: Hearing such unequalled words spoken by the spectators in this manner, Kuntī's chest became wet with tears mingled with perspiration.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā pūrṇaśrutir athābravīt dhṛtarāṣṭro naraśreṣṭho viduraṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ
english: At that great sound, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the best of men whose hearing was full of it, spoke to Vidura with a joyful heart:

sanskrit: kṣattaḥ kṣubdhārṇavanibhaḥ kim eṣa sumahāsvanaḥ sahasaivotthito raṅge bhindann iva nabhastalam
english: "O Kṣattṛ, what is this very great sound like a churning ocean that has suddenly arisen in the arena, as if rending the vault of heaven?"

sanskrit: vidura uvāca eṣa pārtho mahārāja phalgunaḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ avatīrṇaḥ sakavacas tatraiṣa sumahāsvanaḥ
english: Vidura said: O great king, this is Pārtha Phalguna, the joy of Pāṇḍu, who has descended into the arena with his armor on — this is the source of that very great sound.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi rakṣito 'smi mahāmate pṛthāraṇisamudbhūtais tribhiḥ pāṇḍavavahnibhiḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I am fortunate, I am blessed, I am protected, O greatly wise one, by those three fires of the Pāṇḍavas sprung from the kindling sticks of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin samudite raṅge kathaṃ cit paryavasthite darśayām āsa bībhatsur ācāryād astralāghavam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the arena had grown noisy and then somehow settled, Bībhatsu displayed his skill with weapons, surpassing even the teacher.

sanskrit: āgneyenāsṛjad vahniṃ vāruṇenāsṛjat payaḥ vāyavyenāsṛjad vāyuṃ pārjanyenāsṛjad ghanān
english: With the Āgneya weapon he created fire; with the Varuṇa weapon he created water; with the Vāyavya weapon he created wind; with the Parjanya weapon he created clouds.

sanskrit: bhaumena prāviśad bhūmiṃ pārvatenāsṛjad girīn antardhānena cāstreṇa punar antarhito 'bhavat
english: With the Bhauma weapon he sank into the earth; with the Parvata weapon he conjured mountains; and with the weapon of invisibility he vanished from sight once more.

sanskrit: kṣaṇāt prāṃśuḥ kṣaṇād dhrasvaḥ kṣaṇāc ca rathadhūrgataḥ kṣaṇena rathamadhyasthaḥ kṣaṇenāvāpatan mahīm
english: In one moment he was tall, in the next he was short; in one moment he was at the chariot shaft, in the next he stood in the middle of the chariot, and the next instant he alighted on the ground.

sanskrit: sukumāraṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca guruṃ cāpi gurupriyaḥ sauṣṭhavenābhisaṃyuktaḥ so 'vidhyad vividhaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: He who was dear to his teacher, endowed with perfect form, pierced with various arrows both the delicate and fine targets, and also the heavy ones.

sanskrit: bhramataś ca varāhasya lohasya pramukhe samam pañca bāṇān asaṃsaktān sa mumocaikabāṇavat
english: Into the mouth of an iron boar as it revolved, he loosed five arrows in rapid succession without a pause, as if they were a single arrow.

sanskrit: gavye viṣāṇakośe ca cale rajjvavalambite nicakhāna mahāvīryaḥ sāyakān ekaviṃśatim
english: Into a swinging leather ball suspended on a rope, that hero of great valor drove twenty-one arrows.

sanskrit: ity evamādi sumahat khaḍge dhanuṣi cābhavat gadāyāṃ śastrakuśalo darśanāni vyadarśayat
english: He who was skilled in weapons thus displayed such great and varied feats with sword, with bow, and with mace.

sanskrit: tataḥ samāptabhūyiṣṭhe tasmin karmaṇi bhārata mandībhūte samāje ca vāditrasya ca nisvane
english: Then, O Bhārata, when those feats were mostly concluded and the noise of the assembly and the sound of the instruments had died down,

sanskrit: dvāradeśāt samudbhūto māhātmya balasūcakaḥ vajraniṣpeṣasadṛśaḥ śuśruve bhujanisvanaḥ
english: from the direction of the gate arose the sound of slapping arms, indicating great power and prowess, resembling the crash of a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: dīryante kiṃ nu girayaḥ kiṃ svid bhūmir vidīryate kiṃ svid āpūryate vyoma jalabhāraghanair ghanaiḥ
english: "Are the mountains splitting? Is the earth cracking open? Is the sky being filled with clouds heavy with rain?"

sanskrit: raṅgasyaivaṃ matir abhūt kṣaṇena vasudhādhipa dvāraṃ cābhimukhāḥ sarve babhūvuḥ prekṣakās tadā
english: Such was the sudden thought of the arena, O lord of the earth, and at that moment all the spectators turned toward the gate.

sanskrit: pañcabhir bhrātṛbhiḥ pārthair droṇaḥ parivṛto babhau pañcatāreṇa saṃyuktaḥ sāvitreṇeva candramāḥ
english: Droṇa, surrounded by the five Pārtha brothers, shone like the moon in the solar constellation attended by five bright stars.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmnā ca sahitaṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ śatam ūrjitam duryodhanam amitraghnam utthitaṃ paryavārayat
english: The mighty hundred brothers together with Aśvatthāman encircled the risen Duryodhana, slayer of foes.

sanskrit: sa tais tadā bhrātṛbhir udyatāyudhair; vṛto gadāpāṇir avasthitaiḥ sthitaḥ babhau yathā dānavasaṃkṣaye purā; puraṃdaro devagaṇaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ
english: He, standing there with mace in hand, surrounded by those brothers with weapons raised and arrayed around him, shone as Indra, the destroyer of cities, once surrounded by the host of gods at the time of the destruction of the demons.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca datte 'vakāśe puruṣair vismayotphullalocanaiḥ viveśa raṅgaṃ vistīrṇaṃ karṇaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Given way by men whose eyes were wide with astonishment, Karṇa, the conqueror of enemy cities, entered the vast arena.

sanskrit: sahajaṃ kavacaṃ bibhrat kuṇḍaloddyotitānanaḥ sadhanur baddhanistriṃśaḥ pādacārīva parvataḥ
english: Wearing the armor he was born with, his face radiant with his natural earrings, bow in hand, sword fastened at his side, he walked on foot like a moving mountain.

sanskrit: kanyāgarbhaḥ pṛthuyaśāḥ pṛthāyāḥ pṛthulocanaḥ tīkṣṇāṃśor bhāskarasyāṃśaḥ karṇo 'rigaṇasūdanaḥ
english: Born of a maiden's womb, of wide fame, broad-eyed son of Pṛthā, a ray of the sharp-rayed sun god — Karṇa, the destroyer of enemy hosts.

sanskrit: siṃharṣabhagajendrāṇāṃ tulyavīryaparākramaḥ dīptikāntidyutiguṇaiḥ sūryendujvalanopamaḥ
english: Equal in valor and heroic power to lion, bull, and lordly elephant, comparable in his qualities of blazing radiance, beauty, and brilliance to the sun, the moon, and fire.

sanskrit: prāṃśuḥ kanakatālābhaḥ siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā asaṃkhyeyaguṇaḥ śrīmān bhāskarasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ
english: Tall, with the complexion of a golden palm tree, with the build of a lion, a youth of innumerable virtues, auspicious and glorious, born of the self of the sun god.

sanskrit: sa nirīkṣya mahābāhuḥ sarvato raṅgamaṇḍalam praṇāmaṃ droṇakṛpayor nātyādṛtam ivākarot
english: That long-armed hero, having surveyed the entire arena all around, made his salutation to Droṇa and Kṛpa as though without much reverence.

sanskrit: sa sāmājajanaḥ sarvo niścalaḥ sthiralocanaḥ ko 'yam ity āgatakṣobhaḥ kautūhalaparo 'bhavat
english: All the assembled people became still and steady-eyed, overtaken by the excitement of "Who is this?" and full of curiosity.

sanskrit: so 'bravīn meghadhīreṇa svareṇa vadatāṃ varaḥ bhrātā bhrātaram ajñātaṃ sāvitraḥ pākaśāsanim
english: That best of speakers spoke in a voice deep as a thunder-cloud — an unknown brother addressing his brother, as the sun speaks to Indra.

sanskrit: pārtha yat te kṛtaṃ karma viśeṣavad ahaṃ tataḥ kariṣye paśyatāṃ nṝṇāṃ mātmanā vismayaṃ gamaḥ
english: "O Pārtha, whatever remarkable feat you have performed, I shall surpass it before the eyes of all these men — do not be amazed at yourself."

sanskrit: asamāpte tatas tasya vacane vadatāṃ vara yantrotkṣipta iva kṣipram uttasthau sarvato janaḥ
english: Even before that speech of his was finished, O best of speakers, the crowd sprang up swiftly all around as if hurled by a catapult.

sanskrit: prītiś ca puruṣavyāghra duryodhanam athāspṛśat hrīś ca krodhaś ca bībhatsuṃ kṣaṇenānvaviśac ca ha
english: O tiger among men, delight then touched Duryodhana, while shame and anger entered Bībhatsu in an instant.

sanskrit: tato droṇābhyanujñātaḥ karṇaḥ priyaraṇaḥ sadā yat kṛtaṃ tatra pārthena tac cakāra mahābalaḥ
english: Then Karṇa, who always loved battle, permitted by Droṇa, performed with great strength everything that Pārtha had done there.

sanskrit: atha duryodhanas tatra bhrātṛbhiḥ saha bhārata karṇaṃ pariṣvajya mudā tato vacanam abravīt
english: Then Duryodhana, together with his brothers, O Bhārata, embraced Karṇa there with joy and spoke these words:

sanskrit: svāgataṃ te mahābāho diṣṭyā prāpto 'si mānada ahaṃ ca kururājyaṃ ca yatheṣṭam upabhujyatām
english: "Welcome to you, O long-armed one! By good fortune you have arrived, O giver of honor. Both I and the kingdom of the Kurus are yours to enjoy as you wish."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca kṛtaṃ sarveṇa me 'nyena sakhitvaṃ ca tvayā vṛṇe dvandvayuddhaṃ ca pārthena kartum icchāmi bhārata
english: Karṇa said: All else has been accomplished for me; I choose your friendship. And I wish to fight a single combat with Pārtha, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca bhuṅkṣva bhogān mayā sārdhaṃ bandhūnāṃ priyakṛd bhava durhṛdāṃ kuru sarveṣāṃ mūrdhni pādam ariṃdama
english: Duryodhana said: Enjoy pleasures together with me, be the delight of kinsmen, and place your foot on the heads of all ill-wishers, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kṣiptam ivātmānaṃ matvā pārtho 'bhyabhāṣata karṇaṃ bhrātṛsamūhasya madhye 'calam iva sthitam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Pārtha, feeling as though his self had been thrown down, addressed Karṇa who stood in the midst of the group of brothers like an immovable mountain.

sanskrit: anāhūtopasṛptānām anāhūtopajalpinām ye lokās tān hataḥ karṇa mayā tvaṃ pratipatsyase
english: "O Karṇa, the worlds that await those who come uninvited and speak uninvited — those worlds shall be yours, slain by me."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca raṅgo 'yaṃ sarvasāmānyaḥ kim atra tava phalguna vīryaśreṣṭhāś ca rājanyā balaṃ dharmo 'nuvartate
english: Karṇa said: This arena is open to all; what claim do you have here, O Phalguna? For those of royal blood who are supreme in valor, might follows righteousness.

sanskrit: kiṃ kṣepair durbalāśvāsaiḥ śaraiḥ kathaya bhārata guroḥ samakṣaṃ yāvat te harāmy adya śiraḥ śaraiḥ
english: What use are taunts that give comfort only to the weak? Speak with arrows, O Bhārata — I shall sever your head with arrows today in the presence of the teacher.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato droṇābhyanujñātaḥ pārthaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ bhrātṛbhis tvarayāśliṣṭo raṇāyopajagāma tam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Pārtha, the conqueror of enemy cities, permitted by Droṇa, embraced by his brothers who urged him on in haste, advanced toward him for battle.
